slides.title: Eight experiments, one evidence trail
body: Week 09 / H3 / 60-minute lab
Keep the reference run and explain each change.
slides.teach: H3 is entirely practice. Restore the H2 runtime, or run the exercise walkthrough once in a fresh runtime. Tasks 1, 3 and 4 were already calculated by hand in H1; briefly verify them with code. Alternate driver and reviewer after Task 5.

slides.title: Plan the lab before touching code
body: Core tasks first; optional challenges last.
Leave time for replay and explain-back.
slides.teach: The 60-minute lab prioritizes all eight core tasks, then replay, peer explanation and export. Optional challenges may use spare time, not add required homework. If behind, ask for help with the stopping checks instead of bypassing assertions.

slides.title: Restore the exact experiment identity
body: Check the selected candidate and data hash.
Do not regenerate data with a fresh seed.
slides.teach: If using a fresh runtime, run the complete walkthrough in order. A plot cannot restore a fitted model. Inspect the actual selected candidate and computed CSV hash; never paste the reference hash and claim the file was checked.

slides.title: Check Task 1 against your hand result
body: The aggregate changes from 1.9 to 3.25.
The group losses remain 1 and 10.
slides.teach: Compare Task 1 with the original written prediction. Expected values are 1.9 and 3.25. If wrong, review group weights and denominators. Do not rewrite the prediction to hide a mistake; explaining the correction is the learning evidence.

slides.title: Check Task 3 against your derivation
body: The finite grid has 101 endpoint-inclusive points.
Its MAE scales by L squared.
slides.teach: Run Task 3 and check that both grids have 101 points. The bars show defined analytic grid values, not fitted model results. Explain why 0.34 differs from continuous-uniform expectation 1/3, and why the factor 9 is not universal for trained models.

slides.title: Check Task 4 with intermediate sums
body: Appending an error changes n as well as sums.
Use n=5 for the second set.
slides.teach: Run Task 4 and verify the two sums before dividing. Initial n=4; after appending n=5. Expected MAEs are 0.15 and 0.72. Expected RMSEs are sqrt(0.025) and sqrt(1.82). Stop if the denominator or order of operations is wrong.

slides.title: Finish Task 2 without tuning the model
body: Boundary sweeps are exploratory diagnosis.
Keep final-model selection unchanged.
slides.teach: Reuse the Task 2 result from H2 rather than running the entire notebook again. The reviewer checks that each pair of counts sums to 75. Keep the validation-selected model fixed and label the slice sweep exploratory.

slides.title: Task 5: predict a controlled perturbation
body: Increase only x0 by 0.5.
Predict the function change before execution.
slides.teach: Use the original-space x0 coefficient, not the standardized Ridge coefficient. No labels are needed for this function check. Both declared models are additive and linear in x0, so the same x0 perturbation gives the same prediction change for every row.

slides.title: Recover the original-space coefficients
body: Standardized z = (x - mean)/scale.
The raw coefficient is beta/scale.
slides.teach: Derive the equations by substituting z=(x-mean)/scale into beta*z+b. The quadratic feature has its own scaler mean and scale after basis expansion. Include every transformed feature when recovering the original-space intercept.

slides.title: Task 5: verify the equality numerically
body: Compare observed changes with the equation.
Stop if the tolerance check fails.
slides.teach: Locate the runnable Task 5 assertion in the notebook. The reviewer confirms x0 is the only changed column. Passing the check establishes consistency of the fitted function explanation, not physical validity of a target mechanism.

slides.title: Task 6: predeclare a new stress scale
body: Add severity 2.0 with paired rows and noise.
Do not refit or reselect.
slides.teach: Write a prediction before Task 6. Scale 2.0 is a new declared lab extension beyond the three reference conditions; it is not the original final test. Keep its observations separate and preserve the original reference ZIP.

slides.title: Task 6: prove parameters stayed fixed
body: A stress test calls predict, not fit.
Compare saved parameter arrays exactly.
slides.teach: The saved snapshot includes Ridge coefficients and intercept plus scaler means and scales. Stress prediction must not modify them. If the assertion fails, the comparison no longer isolates the input change; investigate rather than deleting the assertion.

slides.title: Record both models, not only the winner
body: Retain n, MAE and RMSE at scale 2.0.
Explain the observed difference in basis terms.
slides.teach: Record both actual candidate metrics and n=150 from Task 6. Explain the difference using representation of x1 squared. Blank fields or pasted reference values do not count as results of the student experiment.

slides.title: Task 7: change bytes, preserve rows
body: Copy the CSV; append one blank line.
Predict the hash and parsed-row outcomes.
slides.teach: Operate only on a copy of the CSV. Appending one blank line changes exact bytes and SHA-256 while the parser recovers the same nonempty records. This distinguishes representation identity from semantic row equality.

slides.title: Task 7: test the distinction explicitly
body: Verify the original hash is unchanged.
Verify all 500 parsed rows still agree.
slides.teach: Run Task 7 and check different copy hash, identical parsed rows and unchanged original hash. A hash acts on bytes, while parsing produces records. Neither check establishes scientific validity or label correctness.

slides.title: Task 8: keep inputs, change the rule
body: Reverse the coefficient of x0 only.
Keep observations and models otherwise fixed.
payload: Same X, same noise, different P(Y|X)
slides.teach: Task 8 stipulates a changed synthetic mechanism; it does not discover it from observations. Inputs, noise and predictions remain fixed, but targets change. Predict identical histograms before running the error comparison.

slides.title: Task 8: expose a monitoring blind spot
body: An identical input histogram sees no change.
Compare errors using the changed outcomes.
slides.teach: Read actual before/after metrics for both candidates in Task 8. The exact same inputs make input-only checks blind to this constructed shift. Do not generalize to a theorem that every possible concept change always worsens MAE.

slides.title: State a limited, evidence-backed claim
body: Name the population and exact change.
Do not claim real-world reliability from synthetic data.
slides.teach: Ask students to rewrite one claim: under these specified paired synthetic stress conditions, this frozen candidate produced these actual metrics. Name the data hash and a limitation. The goal is precision, not an unsupported broad robustness claim.

slides.title: Replay from CSV, not hidden state
body: Load rows and their saved split labels.
Clone the selected candidate and fit train only.
slides.teach: Rerun the CSV replay cell without changing model selection. A clone retains hyperparameters but fits new parameter state on the saved training rows. Exact split membership and feature order matter. Instructor QA also used fresh CPU kernels.

slides.title: A reproducibility check needs a tolerance
body: Compare prediction vectors, not screenshots.
This notebook uses 1e-10 absolute and relative tolerance.
slides.teach: Record the actual maximum prediction difference. This test uses absolute and relative tolerances of 1e-10; it does not promise bit-identical results across every platform. Investigate data precision, versions, splits and feature order before changing tolerances.

slides.title: Use AI to explain, not invent evidence
body: Ask for a hypothesis or a code explanation.
Check every proposed claim against actual outputs.
slides.teach: No paid AI is needed. Students may ask for hypotheses or explanations, then check every claim against actual data, signs, axes and outputs. Record material assistance and verification. AI-generated numbers are not experiment evidence.

slides.title: Optional A: test symmetry of the function
body: The true x1-squared term is even.
A small fitted odd term can break perfect symmetry.
slides.teach: Optional A: both declared candidates contain an odd linear x1 term; the quadratic candidate additionally contains an even square. Flipping x1 isolates the odd term with delta f=-2*raw_beta_x1*x1. The code checks actual function differences.

slides.title: Optional B: simulate an encoding bug
body: Multiply served x0 by 100, leaving targets fixed.
Decode it before calling the same model.
slides.teach: Optional B: these inputs are dimensionless, so call the example an encoding mismatch analogous to a unit error, not an actual physical unit conversion. Check degraded predictions after encoding and restored predictions after correct decoding.

slides.title: Export explanations, not only plots
body: Fill eight predictions and explanations.
Add controlled change, limitation and AI disclosure.
slides.teach: The published response fields start blank. There are eight predictions, eight explanations and three final reflections. Completing fields is only a completeness check, not a correctness grade. Optional challenge answers are not required for core completion.

slides.title: A draft export is still useful evidence
body: Blank explanations produce status draft.
Do not mislabel incomplete work as complete.
slides.teach: After editing responses, rerun only the final export cell. Rerunning initialization erases answers. Missing explanations produce draft status; nonempty fields produce ready for peer discussion. Preserve the reference and exercise ZIPs separately.

slides.title: Peer review: change one role, not the data
body: Reviewer explains a failure without running code.
Driver locates the matching evidence.
slides.teach: The reviewer asks about Task 6 or Task 8, and the driver locates one matching numerical observation and the invariant checks. If evidence cannot be found, repair the record before claiming completion. No graded weekly submission is added.

slides.title: Choose a sensible next experiment
body: A residual pattern suggests a testable change.
A new claim needs a new evaluation protocol.
slides.teach: Connect the observed failure to a declared next hypothesis and evaluation protocol. Fresh grouped external observations or newly collected outcomes may be appropriate; repeatedly recycling the final test is not fresh evidence. This connects to Week 10.

slides.title: What did you prove, and what not?
body: You checked one synthetic workflow and its replay.
You did not validate a real deployed system.
slides.teach: Ask each pair to repair one overclaim using their actual result. Software execution, function consistency and synthetic stress performance are different from causal discovery, external validation and deployment safety.

slides.title: Summary: predict, test, explain, preserve
body: Slice errors; freeze models; probe shift.
Replay exact inputs and bound your claim.
slides.teach: Retrieve the main checks without reading: slices with counts, frozen parameters, exact CSV replay and a bounded evidence card. Ask for one specific assertion rather than vague words such as trustworthy. Challenges remain optional.

slides.title: Exit: a two-minute explain-back
body: Show one result, its mechanism and its limit.
Keep both ZIPs for the workflow studio.
slides.teach: Close with claim, evidence, limitation and next test. Keep both ZIPs for the workflow studio. If incomplete, preserve honest draft status and seek guidance; do not turn the lab into a new graded homework requirement.
